svg.title: Example with made-up inputs: landed cost of three clothing orders
svg.desc: Example with made-up inputs. A US-made cotton T-shirt with a $35 value for duty sent by courier, an Asia-made jacket with a $120 value for duty shipped by courier from a US warehouse, and a US-made synthetic parka with a $300 value for duty. Each bar splits into item value, surtax at 50 percent of value for duty only when the goods are US-origin and the line is listed, customs duty, and GST at 5 percent of value for tax. Provincial sales tax is not shown.
svg.text: Example with made-up inputs: three courier orders
Bar length is Canadian dollars. GST uses the 5 percent rate in Customs Notice 26-23. Provincial tax is not in the bars.
Customs duty is $0 on all three rows
Scale: $1 = 1 px, so the $300 item is 300 px and the $150 surtax is 150 px. The $2.63 GST segment is 2.6 px.
Parka total on this method: $300 + $150 + $0 + $22.50 GST = $472.50. GST segment sits past the 650 px mark and is labelled here.
Surtax is 50 percent only on the two US-origin rows, and only if the garment is classified on Schedule 3. The jacket has no surtax.
The $35 row is under the $40 courier band, which remits ordinary sales tax. How that remission combines with surtax is check with CBSA or your carrier.
Duty is $0 here because of the courier band or, for US-origin goods, UST Free on these lines. Confirm classification and UST with CBSA.
Saving Optimizer. Example with made-up inputs. Checked 29 Sep 2026. Not a courier invoice.
